To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the probability of a numeral response is a function of the position of the numeral stimulus word in the stimulus list and the number of intervening stimulus words, (2) the probability of an associative response is a function, in part, of the idiodynamic set of the S, and (3) the probability of the occurrence of an associative response to a stimulus word is a function, at least in part, of a stimulus characteristic of the word, viz., its frequency of occurrence.
the effects of stimulus words on the probability of their associates depend on the order of occurrence in a list, and the position of an intervening word in the stimulus list.
the effects of stimulus characteristics and individual differences in idiodynamic set on associative responding are additive.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of idiodynamic sets and stimulus characteristics on word association behavior.
the effects of stimulus and response characteristics on word association responses.
the effects of stimulus characteristics and individual differences in a contrast logical idiodynamic set on the occurrence of numeral homonym associates.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

word association responses, in general, are determined by the interplay between transient stimulus effects (e.g., the position of an ambiguous word in a stimulus list) and enduring characteristics of the individual Ss.

the results obtained are in accord with the general theory that word associations are determined by the simultaneous interaction of stimulus effects and idiodynamic factors, and that these factors are not mutually exclusive, but are interdependent in a complex manner.
word association responses result from the interaction between the stimulus effects of the words presented to the Ss and the enduring characteristics of the Ss.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
word association responses can be predicted from the combination of a stimulus characteristic and an idiodynamic set.
the idiodynamics of the S are important in determining the effects of stimulus characteristics on verbal behavior.
we have shown that the word association response is determined by the interaction of the characteristics of the stimulus and enduring characteristics of the individual.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a strong relationship between individual differences and word associations.
we need to be more careful in how we use the term “idiodynamic.”
we can use the idiodynamic set as a way to predict individual responses to certain stimuli.
